The result stays -- it is the ceiling block and the headline, not the pipeline's output. The ledger denominator, the backend-error attrition, the single-outcome-stratum admission and the confounding-by-indication note are now rendered nowhere; they remain in metrics.json under observed, reads.attrition and reads.one_cell; 2026-09-10 fifth pass: restored Retriever above Intake in the stages array. f32630a (2026-09-09, operator-requested) put Retriever first because the reader's sequence -- type, retrieve, then ask what was really encoded -- differs from the pipeline's internal sequence; 5c02e78's adversarial-review rewrite reverted the array to intake-first without mentioning the order in its commit message, while leaving index.html's liveIntakePanel wiring from the same original fix untouched. The sentence above reading 'stage order is the pipeline's, not the order the page was built in' describes the pre-f32630a rationale and is superseded by this one: order is now the reader's, not the pipeline's | 2026-09-15: the `retriever` stage became `ask`. A standalone cosine panel is not a stage a reader can act on — the rail now names what the stop DOES, and the retrieval facts are evidence inside it. No figure changed and no panel was deleted: `retrieverPanel` still renders a selected example, which is all the static page can show, and it is where abstention is demonstrated. | 2026-09-15: intake's `does` rewritten for a reader who has not read the code. It named the FIELDS without saying what they are, so `construct` and `population` meant nothing to a visitor. Each field is now glossed. The matching step is attributed to Ask on purpose: intake runs no encoder and computes no cosine, and the role it records is the one thing it promises never to use.

stages.name: Ask
stages.sub: your question → candidates → the model assigns the roles · you confirm the pair
does: Retrieves a candidate pool with a fine-tuned bge-small encoder: argmax cosine over precomputed target vectors, fp32 CPU, no language-model call and no network
Abstains when the top cosine falls below the shipped threshold, and refuses to serve at all if the dictionary hash does not match
Then a language model reads your question AND that pool and assigns the exposure and the outcome, selecting BY INDEX so it can never write a key
Proposes a pair and stops. One vector cannot represent a causal direction, so a two-construct question is the model's to decompose — and yours to confirm
stages.placeholder: Will show a real run: the candidate pool with its cosines, the role the model gave each one, and the threshold and abstention behind them, with every target pseudonymised.

stages.name: Intake
stages.sub: what you typed → the one query string the search model sees · no language-model call
does: Turns what you typed into the ONE query string the search model will actually see. Plain string concatenation: the same fields give the same query every time, with no language model and no network.
request — your words, exactly as you typed them. construct — what is being searched for, and the only part the search model ever reads.

role — whether you wanted this to be an exposure or an outcome. It is recorded and then DELIBERATELY left out of the query: the search model turns your words into a single point in space and has no notion of cause and effect, so telling it the role would change nothing it does.
instances — concrete examples you named. One is dropped as covered when all of its content words already appear in the construct, so the same word is not searched for twice.
population — left empty by the shipped contract, so nothing here narrows the search to a subgroup.

rendered query — the finished string, assembled as [population] construct [timeframe][: instance, instance, …]. Comparing it against the instrument, and deciding which match is the exposure and which the outcome, happens at Ask, not here.
stages.placeholder: Will show the real RetrievalRequest and the string the shipped template rendered for it.

stages.name: Generate
stages.sub: S1 enumerate · S2 prune · S3 estimability · then the Specifier
does: S1 enumerates candidate exposure–outcome pairs over distinct constructs
S2 prunes on construct identity, battery membership, free text
S3 screens estimability: blocked until two survey metadata exports arrive
Runs the Specifier on a pair it produced, rather than one you typed
stages.placeholder: Will show the gate's real output: how many pairs were live, passed and blocked, and which exports are missing.

stages.name: Specifier
stages.sub: adjudicate → reason → gate → structure → dictionary authority → validate → rank
does: A deterministic adjudication step runs before the first call and gives the same answer for every attempt
The language model reasons with dictionary lookups and stops when it stops looking things up, or at a step ceiling
A gate checks that the required lookups appear in the log, not that the prose claims them
Every field the dictionary can compute is overwritten from the dictionary, and stale rationales are dropped
Ranking is a fixed function of the record: no judge, no self-rating
stages.placeholder: The stage itself ran once, with the estimability gate switched off. Its reasoning log and the record it produced are not on this page. Will show a real reasoning log beside the record it produced, keys pseudonymised the same way as the retriever runs.
stages.waits_for: a redacted copy of the scored run's records: they carry instrument wording and variable keys, which this page cannot show. The Metrics tab reports how many there were, not what they say

stages.name: Record
does: Carries the full wording for every variable, never a bare key
Stamps estimability, so an unverifiable design cannot read as a verified one
Names the analysis model, its unit of analysis and any clustering; there is no study-design field, so a record cannot say cross-sectional or cohort
Rejects a mediator placed in the adjusted list by the role it was given, not by any causal graph: no typed DAG exists
Has no critique seam; a refusal is a separate record carrying its reason and what would unblock it
stages.placeholder: The stage itself emitted records once, with the estimability gate switched off, and the Metrics tab counts them. Will show a real record: full wording per variable, the estimability stamp, and the covariates adjusted, excluded and sought.
stages.waits_for: the same redacted copy; the records exist and are counted on the Metrics tab

stages.name: Score
stages.sub: match rate vs held-out published findings · contamination verdicts
does: Scores committed records against a key held on a branch the pipeline never sees
Refuses to score anything generated where the key was reachable
Reports match rate only beside contamination and leakage verdicts
Runs exactly once, on a tag, before any tuning, so it cannot become a feedback signal
stages.placeholder: Will show the generation clone's GenerationEnv stamp and the one scored run.

stages.name: Metrics
stages.sub: the one scored run · its ceiling, its bibliography, what it establishes
does: States the ceiling before the score, because the score is unreadable without it
Says how the scored set was produced, gate off, before showing what it scored
Lists the cohort papers the run was scored against, and what each one is
Does not report the pipeline's own output: the per-record listing and the run's counts are its end-to-end check, and read as evidence
Carries the retrieval measurements and their known limitations
